text.p: Browning-Ferris Industries Inc. said on Thursday it will take a special pre-tax charge of $447 million for the sale of its Italian operations, other divestments and asset write-downs.
The Houston-based international waste services company said it would take the charge, equal to $1.80 a share, when it reports its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings next Thursday.
Excluding the charge, the company said it expected to post earnings of 33 cents a share, just a penny shy of Wall Street estimates according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.

The company said the big charge resulted from a management decision to sell the firm's Italian operations, divest certain domestic and international non-core business assets and operations and close some facilities that were not expected to reach performance targets.

Browning-Ferris also said it planned to cut capital spending in fiscal 1997 to about $790 million from an estimated $1.2 billion in fiscal 1996. It said it would spend about $690 million in North America and $100 million in international markets.
The company said the special charge also included a writedown to fair value of its investment in a landfill in Azusa, Calif.

"This writedown is the result of the changing competitive nature of waste disposal in the Los Angeles market area and the continuing negative legal climate, including recent adverse decisions by the California judicial and regulatory authorities, bearing on the site's ability to accept municipal solid waste," the company said.
Officials of the company were not immediately available to comment further.
Browning's revised financial goals included maintaining a strong credit rating and increasing profits at a faster pace than revenues, it said.
The company changed its annual and long-term compensation plans to meet these goals, it added.
Browning-Ferris stock rose $1.125 to $26.75 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
